Finding round: **graded, promoted to `pm:queue`**, `finding` shed. Routed **`domain:spec`** (`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` — that package is one lane including its shipped text). Filed correctly rather than ridden along on #11993, which holds zero `packages/spec`.

Type **Bug**, not Task, and the filer's own "cosmetic" framing undersells it: the entries mix **U+002C and U+3002 inside a single sentence**. That is not a house-style preference anyone chose — it is incorrect Chinese typography, and it ships to a business user in a toast. This seat typed the two objectui copy findings this round (#6610 ar, #6611 de) the same way, so the treatment is consistent across all three.

⭐ **The propagation argument is what makes it worth doing now rather than eventually.** The catalog is explicitly the seat every *future* refusal is meant to land in — so whatever punctuation it uses becomes the platform's de-facto house style, copied outward by every subsequent entry. Nine keys is a cheap pass; ninety is not. And the two surfaces genuinely sit together on one screen: an approval action's description renders full-width (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/translations/zh-CN.objects.generated.ts`, U+FF0C / U+FF1F) while a refusal from the same feature renders ASCII.

⚠️ **Clause-② path leg fires** — the diff touches `packages/spec/src/**`, and the path leg is independent of content, so it does not care that this is text-only. Dispatched below the contract-review tier, it is ⛔ not enqueueable without `needs:contract-review`. Same note as #12722 this round; the spec seat should pick the tier deliberately. ⛔ This seat does not attach the gate label — that is the dispatching seat's action at enqueue time.

⚠️ **Cross-lane read-coupling, and this is the part that will bite if unstated.** The fix moves string literals that two pin tests quote:

- `packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.test.ts` (quotes at least one) — same lane, moves in the same PR.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/recall-refusal-user-copy.test.ts` — **`domain:services`**, landing with **#11993**, and it quotes the recall sentence as the operator-visible pin.

⇒ The file surfaces do not intersect, so a batch-independence check would clear these two — but a pin in the services lane **asserts the exact literal this card changes**. Whichever lands second turns the other red for no real reason. ⛔ Do not fix that by editing a pin's expectation to match new output. The order that works: #11993's pin lands first, then this card moves the literal **and** that pin together in one PR, declaring the cross-lane file in its claim. If this card somehow goes first, #11993's dev must be told to write the pin against the **new** punctuation — ⛔ not against the sentence as quoted in either card body.

Also in the same cluster this round: **#12716** (approvals recall visible-predicate, `domain:services`, queued this round) touches the same feature though not these literals. Three cards now converge on `approval_recall`; the services and spec seats should compare notes before dispatching any of them.

**Scope as filed**: `zh-CN` block only — English, `ja-JP` and `es-ES` rows are unaffected. All five situation keys plus the four `delete_restricted*` variants share the pattern. Measured on `origin/main` at `15bf9e859`; re-verify at dispatch, since #11993's pin may have landed meanwhile.

Dedup confirmed: **#12081** (closed) was ASCII commas in re-wrapped Chinese *prose* in doc source with soft-break rendering — same character, different surface and different cause. ⛔ Not a duplicate.
